title.narrative: Strengthened AML/CFT regulatory and supervisory capacity of DNFBPs, through the development of AML/CFT supervisory or regulatory tools and guidelines in Ethiopia
Number of developed and adopted revised AML/CFT guidelines for the sector, particularly 1 STR guideline for DNFBPs reviewed and updated as per the FATF Recommendations.
The revision and update of the national/sectoral risk assessment, or relevant AML/CFT laws, regulations, policies, or strategies in Ethiopia.

Number of laws, regulations, policies or strategies reviewed with recommendations for improvement and enhancement in Ethiopia. Particularly, 1 comprehensive SOP for investigation of ML and CFT developed for high-risk crimes 1 revised national ML/TF risk assessment/sectoral risk assessment based on the recommendations from the upcoming mutual evaluation of Ethiopia.
Enhanced Inter-Agency Cooperation and Coordination among AML/CFT stakeholders through structured multi-agency meetings, joint strategic planning, and formalized information exchange mechanisms.

Number of formalized inter-agency information-sharing protocols developed, adopted, and operationalized among AML/CFT stakeholders. Particularly, One inter-agency information-sharing protocol has been developed, adopted, and operationalised among AML/CFT stakeholders in each jurisdiction.

Strengthened regulatory and supervisory capacity of Kenyas Public Benefits Organisation Regulatory Authority (PBORA) to prevent the abuse of NPOs for terrorism financing, through technical assistance, development of risk-based frameworks, and targeted capacity-building activities.

Number of guidance documents for revising Kenyas NPO regulatory framework developed, incorporating findings and recommendations from the Terrorism Financing Risk Assessment for NPOs. Particularly, 1 guidance document developed for the focused regulation of NPOs
Enhanced Inter-Agency Cooperation and Coordination among AML/CFT stakeholders through structured multi-agency meetings, joint strategic planning, and formalized information exchange mechanisms.

Number of instances in which the FATF and ESAAMLG note positive progress in Kenya and Ethiopias AML/CFT national coordination. Particularly, 1 FATF/ESAAMLG follow-up report indicating positive progress of national coordination in Ethiopia and Kenya.

Strengthened AML/CFT regulatory and supervisory capacity of The Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Kenya (ICPAK) among accounting professionals, through developing supervisory tools in Kenya.
Number of revised AML/CFT guidelines for the accounting sector developed and adopted. Particularly, 1 AML/CFT guideline or the accounting sector document updated.

Strengthened AML/CFT regulatory and supervisory capacity of The Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Kenya (ICPAK) among accounting professionals, through developing supervisory tools in Kenya.
Number of sectoral risk assessments conducted and finalised. Particularly, 1 risk assessment report for the accounting sector developed and adopted
Strengthened capacity of the FIS to conduct operational and strategic analysis, leading to trends and typology reports, which can enable reporting entities to identify suspicious transactions better.

Number of FIS staffs trained on operational and strategic analysis to support the development of trends and typologies reports.
Particularly, 10 FIS staff (5 male, 5 female) trained in operational and strategic analysis and production of AML/CFT typology reports.
Strengthened capacity of PBORA and the ICPAK to regulate better and supervise the NPO and accounting sectors in Kenya to ensure they comply with the FATF AML/CFT standards.

Number of PBORA staff sensitized and trained on their AML/CFT regulatory and supervisory responsibilities and the implementation of UN Security Council Resolutions 1267 and 1373. Particularly, 12 supervisors in PBORA (6 male and 6 female) trained and sensitized

AML/CFT enforcement, regulation and supervision efforts are enhanced in Ethiopia and Kenya, through strengthened policy, legal, and regulatory frameworks, in alignment with FATF recommendations.
Particularly, reforms to a total of 16 legal, regulatory and policy AML/CFT documents for Ethiopia and Kenya
Number of laws, regulations and policy frameworks Ethiopia and Kenya developed that comply with FATF Recommendations.
AML/CFT investigation, prosecution, regulatory and supervisory actions are improved in Kenya and Ethiopia, through building the personnel capacity of responsible bodies to undertake their mandate.

Number of law enforcement, judiciary, regulatory and supervisory actors personnels capacity increased in implementing FATF recommendations. Particularly, A total of 177 supervisors, investigators, judges and FIS staff with increased capacity.
Enhanced Inter-Agency Cooperation and Coordination among AML/CFT stakeholders through structured multi-agency meetings, joint strategic planning, and formalized information exchange mechanisms.

Number of national inter-agency coordination meetings that resulted in agreed follow-up action on ML/TF investigations, prosecutions, seizure of assets or regulatory actions. Particularly, 2 joint investigated cases prosecuted, leading to the recovery of assets in each country.
Strengthened AML/CFT regulatory and supervisory capacity of DNFBPs, through the development of AML/CFT supervisory or regulatory tools and guidelines in Ethiopia

Number of sectoral risk assessments conducted for selected DNFBP sectors Particurlary, 2 sectoral risk assessments conducted in selected sector based on the recommendations from the upcoming mutual evaluation of Ethiopia.

Strengthened capacity of AML/CFT supervisors in Ethiopia to conduct AML/CFT risk-based supervision, including for United Nations Security Council Resolutions related to targeted financial sanctions to ensure compliance with FATF standards

Number of experts trained and mentored, responsible for implementing targeted financial sanctions on implementing the UN Security Council Resolutions on Targeted Financial Sanctions.
Particularly, 20 experts (10 male and 10 female) trained and mentored on the implementation of the UNSCR.
A holistic approach to combat financial crimes is improved through enhanced institutional coordination and collaboration among AML/CFT stakeholders in Kenya and Ethiopia.
Percentage increase in the use of financial intelligence disseminations by ML/FT investigation and prosecution units.

target.value: 50% of Kenyas and 50% of Ethiopias financial intelligence disseminations converted into investigative and prosecutable cases.

title.narrative: Strengthened capacity of the judiciary, investigators and prosecutors to utilize financial intelligence for conducting financial investigations, leading to prosecutions and asset recovery in Ethiopia

Number of law enforcement and prosecution officers trained in a targeted joint training programs on ML/TF identification, investigations, prosecution and asset tracing and forfeiture.
Particularly, 75 investigators (60% male and 40% female), prosecutors and financial analysts trained in financial investigation in Ethiopia.
A holistic approach to combat financial crimes is improved through enhanced institutional coordination and collaboration among AML/CFT stakeholders in Kenya and Ethiopia.

National Coordination and cooperation enhanced as shown by periodic reports from the FATF International Co-operation Review Group (ICRG) or ESAMALG Follow-Up process, indicating that Kenyas or Ethiopias progress in institutional coordination and collaboration.

target.value: Meetings of the national task forces and joint investigations go beyond coordination and showcase the results of prosecutions and the recovery of assets.

title.narrative: The Horn of Africa (HoA) Regions compliance with FATF recommendations and its financial integrity and stability are improved through strengthened national anti-money laundering, combating the financing of terrorism and combating proliferation financing (AML/CFT/CPF) frameworks and their enforcement actions.
Decrease in ML and TF risk score and rating of Ethiopia and Kenya

target.value: The capacity of AML/CFT enforcement, regulatory, and supervisory institutions to combat ML and TF has enhanced, as demonstrated by an increase in legal enforcement and supervisory actions for ML/TF cases and in the adoption and implementation of new and updated policies and laws in compliance with FATF recommendations.

title.narrative: Strengthened regulatory and supervisory capacity of Kenyas Public Benefits Organisation Regulatory Authority (PBORA) to prevent the abuse of NPOs for terrorism financing, through technical assistance, development of risk-based frameworks, and targeted capacity-building activities.

Number of targeted risk-based monitoring frameworks developed for at-risk NPOs, incorporating risk assessment findings and aligned with FATF Recommendation 8 in Kenya. Particularly, 1 monitoring framework developed for NPOs recognised as high risk in line with the FATF definition.
